approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a population of scored molecular graphs. It samples a first parent from score-ranked bands, then either mutates that graph or samples a different scored identity and joins connected fragments from the two parents. Crossover may receive a finishing mutation, and ordinary mutation may continue for several steps. Valid, canonically unique products fill a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to every accepted task-local score, using count fingerprints and a Tanimoto kernel, supplies correlated posterior draws that choose the announced evaluation batch. New real scores update both the complete learning archive and bounded greedy survivors, so accepted offspring can become future breeders. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled in this Parent.
approach.novelty: Remove only the rule that forbids drawing the first parent again as its crossover partner. The original score-ranked partner sampler can then draw the same accepted identity twice, and the existing fragment construction, finishing mutation and duplicate checks decide what happens. Earlier siblings removed crossover, flattened partner rank weights or changed donor cuts; none isolated this identity-exclusion rule. Self recombination could form a different graph, reproduce a rejected parent, or change retry and pool competition. Measuring those outcomes tests whether forced distinct-parent mating contributes under the current complete method.

observed_bottleneck: The unmeasured restriction is the Parent's exclusion of the actual first canonical identity at every crossover-partner draw. This bounds its source combinations; its value or harm is not established by the known value of crossover or rank preference. Parent n-62daf219c70a source calls select_parent(exclude=parent.smiles) only inside the unchanged crossover guard. Its full indexed audits report 34,334 distinct-identity crossover requests, 29,730 pooled crossover products and 1,492 accepted crossover offspring, versus 4,350 total accepted offspring, 629 best-parent beats and 258 sequential incumbent advances. The three actual summary.json and run.log pairs are present and successful: seed macros 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313, mean 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747. Per-task means in frozen task order are 0.43571364694864806, 0.6995902616231001, 0.9989892192705674, 0.2244176914540413 and 0.6196374293709309. Whole-crossover removal n-767d2ce08797 lost 0.054937284705486644, with all seed macros lower but three improved endpoints. Partner-rank removal n-ee95752352ec retained distinct partners and support yet lost 0.05180750887063701, despite 702 versus 629 parent beats, 265 versus 258 incumbent advances and lower seed dispersion; its absolute accepted offspring and generating-parent scores fell. Four endpoint gains and positive zaleplon/median task means remain counterexamples to a uniform-loss description. Compatible-donor n-eb61315a5619 lost 0.020270634588430703 while 22,117 conditioned immediate products reproduced parents and 496 accepted conditioned products obtained novelty only through finishing. Revised donor copy exclusion n-bddb1dbe8e32 raised distinct-immediate evaluations from 1,368 to 1,610 but lost 0.10265273096567833, with five improved endpoints. These controls motivate tracing real products and scores; none tests source-identity self exclusion. The Parent crossover separately draws a large first fragment and a small second fragment, so identical source identities neither force a copy nor establish a useful novel product.
hypothesis: Remove only the selected first canonical identity exclusion from actual crossover-partner sampling, allowing ordinary self-pair draws under the original score-quantile band and member law while preserving all first-parent behavior and unchanged crossover, finishing and admission.

finding_summary.headline: Distinct-parent exclusion contributes: removal lowers the mean by 0.03199 despite productive self offspring
finding_summary.insights:
Enforcing distinct source identities contributes positively under this complete method and evaluation profile, even though self recombination can produce useful, subsequently reused molecules. The tested contribution includes both permitting self-pairs and redistributing probability among other partners, followed by their different random draws and feedback histories. These data do not separate those channels or establish a diversity mechanism.

The extra local wins are especially informative: total parent wins rose from 629 to 673 and incumbent advances from 258 to 265, yet mean accepted-offspring score fell from 0.385256 to 0.371429 and mean best-parent score from 0.470456 to 0.448955. The advances were more numerous but added less total improvement. Thus easier parent comparisons and lower dispersion can accompany weaker endpoints. The molecular assessment also finds different leading aromatic families across seeds alongside recurring questionable attachments and unspecified stereochemistry; those concerns persist in the Parent and do not identify the exclusion rule as their cause. Individual channel contributions, chemical mediation and reliability beyond the measured panel remain unresolved. This result answers the distinct-partner boundary within the retained foundation, without attributing an entire foundation or combining sibling effects.
finding_summary.results:
The removal ran as specified and lowered the complete mean from 0.595670 to 0.563677, a decrease of 0.031992 against the registered 0.002 scale. Ten of the 15 task/seed endpoints fell and five improved. Seed-macro changes were -0.092144, +0.012064 and -0.015897; macro dispersion also fell, from 0.026593 to 0.022045. The largest losses were the seed-0 deco-hop and sitagliptin endpoints, while the zaleplon task mean improved.

There were 2,851 actual self-pairs. They produced 359 immediate copies, 2,489 different graphs and three construction failures. Finishing changed 135 copies into different final identities; 224 remained rejected copies. The self channel reached 2,454 fresh pool entries and 155 real evaluations, including 27 parent wins and 14 incumbent advances. Eighty-seven accepted self products later bred, and 41 had accepted children. Separately, replay from identical sampler states found 6,283 changed choices among nonself partners, which reached 346 accepted evaluations. All 15 full cells had evaluated self products, but 310 individual batches had self draws without a self evaluation; these zeros and terminally censored products remain in the comparison.

molecular.headline: Aromatic families vary across seeds, but reactive attachments, awkward ring closures and unspecified stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: For n-60350f969287, every supplied Child trajectory and every published code-Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectory was read: all five tasks on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 300 observations in each file. Each task has 900 Child observations, including 870 optimizer proposals. There are no missing trajectory paths or uncovered tasks. The immutable brief reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, all supplied seeds matched, and no profile-mismatched seeds. This is a complete chemistry comparison under the frozen Research in Depth epoch-1 profile with feedback batches of 10; the paired endpoints below are copied from observed trajectory maxima and are descriptive. No activation or component-contribution verdict is made. These evaluated structures do not identify which chemistry came from equal-source crossover, ordinary mutation, subsequent finishing, or adaptive selection. The output contains compact fused aromatic ketones, esters and N-amino amides; linked heteroaryl assemblies, including very large repeated structures; diaryl aliphatic amines; bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems; and fluorinated diones and polycycles. Recognizable medicinal chemistry coexists with N-halogen bonds, sulfur-fluoride attachments, unusually cross-linked aromatic-labelled graphs, and unspecified stereochemistry. Different seeds produce different families, while the strongest molecules within a seed often remain close relatives: structural diversity is moderate overall, not global collapse, but independent plausible alternatives among leaders are limited. Ring-closure-string incidence spans 0.9598 to 0.9793, and aromatic-string incidence spans 0.9483 to 0.9782. Those are molecule-level text incidences from the digest, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. All tasks have charged_rate=0.0 and stereocentre_rate=0.0. The neutral strings nevertheless include clearly protonatable amines. Heavy-atom counts and ring descriptions below were read from the actual trajectory graphs with RDKit 2023.09.6; successful parsing is not evidence of stability, accessible geometry, synthesis or biological activity. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 observations, not each seed's retained best, so each full seed trajectory was inspected. Parent evidence was read through the supplied evidence_index, including the full Molecular assessments for n-62daf219c70a and original gap source n-c55c3d520a2c. Their original chemical concerns and counterexamples remain conditional historical evidence; present examples are re-observations, not unchanged structures or independent mechanistic replication. The complete path/hash manifest, descriptor readings and Parent history are in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.slots/round-0024-slot-3/molecular-audit.json, with row-level provenance in molecular-records.jsonl in the same directory. Only Child molecules authorized by the immutable digest or citation_trajectory_paths are included in cited_smiles.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest molecules are compact aromatic/carbonyl assemblies. Seed 0 reaches a 24-heavy-atom benzimidazole-like fused heteroaromatic ketone joined to phenyl, with vinyl, ethyl, methoxy and N-F substitution. Seed 1 reaches a 24-heavy-atom partially unsaturated fused nitrogen ring carrying a pyridyl ester, methyl/vinyl substituents and N-F or N-Br. Seed 2 reaches a 25-heavy-atom indole-like N-amino anilide: a fused aromatic system linked through carbonyl to nitrogen bearing both aryl and terminal amino substitution, with N-halogen on the fused ring. The latter therefore contains a genuine N-N bond, not simply an ordinary anilide. Mean optimizer SMILES length is 41.6, ring-string incidence 0.9632, aromatic-string incidence 0.9586 and halogen-string incidence 0.8943. These are not ring-deficient molecules. Their carbonyl and aromatic frameworks are recognizable, but the frequent N-halogen environments make their synthetic plausibility questionable. Parent leaders instead include an aromatic cumulene/imine in seed 0, an N-hydroxy pyridyl amide in seed 1 and an aryl vicinal diketone in seed 2; the broad aromatic territory persists while the detailed linkages differ.
liabilities: N-F, N-Br and N-Cl attachments to ring nitrogen differ chemically from ordinary carbon-bound aryl halogens; their appearance among leaders is not stability evidence.

The seed-2 N-amino amide introduces N-N chemistry, and nearby molecules alter N-O or N-S environments. Familiar amide-like connectivity does not establish synthetic accessibility of the whole molecule.
Vinyl groups, hydrazine-like substitution and unassigned saturated stereochemistry need molecule-specific assessment; the scores do not justify declaring every such group forbidden.
missing_features: Leading families do not consistently show conventional stable nitrogen substitution while retaining their favorable compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement. An ordinary N-H indole amide is already present initially, so this is a consistency gap rather than inability to represent it.
The potentially stereogenic saturated centre in the seed-1 fused-ring ester is unspecified; the observed score ordering does not establish a stereochemical reward or a preferred stereoisomer.
Chemically independent, plausible alternatives to each seed's leading fused-ring family remain limited. The observations do not identify an exact absent objective-specific pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 ketone and seed-1 ester both reach 0.4484138510190879, and the seed-2 N-amino amide reaches 0.4519753205796759. Methane and the small saturated dioxolane observation score 0.0, so a ring by itself is insufficient. Adding a methyl substituent to the ketone's pendant phenyl lowers its observed score to 0.30133942471759917. Extending one methyl to ethyl in the leading N-amino-amide family lowers the score to 0.30187099911499876. The corresponding unsubstituted pendant phenyl member still scores 0.4339692349432291. The seed-1 N-F and N-Br ester variants tie exactly at 0.4484138510190879; other leading N-halogen variants also tie. The visible association is with the complete compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement and specific substitutions, not monotonically more carbon, more halogen or one uniquely required N-halogen bond. Observed Child versus matched Parent best values are: seed 0, 0.4484138510190879 versus 0.39405142067435733; seed 1, 0.4484138510190879 versus 0.47411701813450596; seed 2, 0.4519753205796759 versus 0.438972502037081. The improvement in seeds 0 and 2 and loss in seed 1 do not isolate a chemical mediator.

per_task.generated_character: The pooled digest leaders are almost entirely the relatively compact seed-2 family, but the other seeds look very different. Seed 2 makes 31- and 32-heavy-atom aryl-pyrazole/pyrimidine assemblies with carbon-bound fluorine/bromine, branched alkyl substitution and an amino-ether methine connecting the heteroaryl regions. That N,O-acetal-like linkage and its unassigned centres still require stability and synthesis assessment. Seed 0's best has 45 heavy atoms: a substituted aryl ester/acylurea-like assembly with N-formyl carbonyls, pyrazole/pyrimidine-like rings and aromatic-labelled fragments containing short internal closures. The graph has four-membered cycles inside those cross-linked fragments; ordinary aromatic labels do not establish ordinary aromatic geometry. An 80-heavy-atom relative repeats more of these carbonyl and heteroaryl units. Seed 1's best is a 70-heavy-atom, six-aryl-ring assembly with pyridyl/diazine regions, imine/enamine connectivity, thioethers and several S-F attachments. These unoxidized sulfur-fluoride environments must not be described as ordinary aryl fluorides or sulfonyl fluorides. Mean proposal SMILES length is 78.4, maximum 218, ring-string incidence 0.9793 and aromatic-string incidence 0.9782. Parent seed 0 instead reaches a compact 30-heavy-atom linked fused nitrogen-carbonyl/thione system, seed 1 a smaller nitrile/cyanate heteroaryl assembly, and seed 2 peroxide-containing aryl/heteroaryl structures. Both sides contain local chemical liabilities; compactness alone does not certify plausibility.
liabilities: Very large repeated heteroaryl assemblies and multiple carbonyl-rich nitrogen linkages create synthesis, conformational and property concerns; graph size and ring count are not evidence of useful chemical breadth.
Short internal bonds in aromatic-labelled aza-ring fragments create four-membered graph cycles whose feasible geometry is not shown.

Seed-1 S-F attachments on unoxidized sulfur are specific reactive-environment concerns. The score comparison also includes an S-methyl alternative, so a particular S-F bond is not universally necessary.
Seed-2 N,O-acetal-like and chlorine-bearing methine centres have unresolved stability and stereochemistry even though the rest of the framework looks more conventional.
missing_features: Seeds 0 and 1 do not establish a compact, conventionally connected version of their favorable heteroaryl/carbonyl or heteroaryl/sulfur arrangements at a higher score; repeated large assemblies are common, while the smaller seed-2 family shows compact generation is possible.
The amino-ether centre and branched alkyl substituent in the seed-2 leaders lack stereochemical definition. The cross-linked aromatic-labelled fragments in seed 0 lack demonstrated credible geometry.

The compact fused nitrogen-carbonyl organization seen in the higher-scoring Parent seed 0 is not recovered among these Child leaders. This is a descriptive coverage difference, not an exact missing pharmacophore or evidence that copying that scaffold is an authorized solution.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dione scores 0.548381482770623, while ethene and the small halogenated alkane example score 0.5. Seed 2's ethoxy and isopropoxy amino-ether analogues, and a further chlorine-bearing variant at the same methine, all reach 0.6115934939464351. Replacing the amino connection with a direct carbon connection in the isopropoxy analogue gives 0.5686721157711376. This supports the observed arrangement and spacing of heteroaryl and amino/ether functions within that family, without proving a universal donor requirement. Seed 0's 45-heavy-atom best reaches 0.6042806936682606; the 80-heavy-atom elaboration reaches 0.6038062283737025, so adding many rings and carbonyls supplies no higher observed reward. Seed 1's 70-heavy-atom best scores 0.6038868483087549; its close S-F rather than S-methyl peripheral variant scores 0.6036935704514363, providing no evidence that every sulfur-fluoride attachment is required. Observed Child versus matched Parent best values are: seed 0, 0.6042806936682606 versus 0.8561477222467935; seed 1, 0.6038868483087549 versus 0.6248206599713055; seed 2, 0.6115934939464351 versus 0.6178024026512013. All Child seed best values lie below their matched Parent values despite the different size and functional-group profiles; this does not establish a size-based cause.

per_task.generated_character: High-scoring output already contains accessible aliphatic amines together with hydrophobic aryl regions. Seed 0's 32-heavy-atom best combines two substituted phenyl groups, methoxy and aniline groups, a partially unsaturated seven-membered amine ring, a tertiary amino side chain and a sulfoxide. Nearby structures carry less conventional multiply bonded sulfur environments. Seed 1's 23-heavy-atom best is a diaryl aminoethyl arrangement with phenol, aryl chlorines and an azetidine; an aziridine relative is also strongly scored. Seed 2's 29-heavy-atom best has fluorinated phenyl regions, phenol/methoxy substituents, an N-methylpyrrolidine side chain, a primary amine and a substituted benzocyclobutene-like region. An earlier open-chain diarylmethylamino/pyrrolidine structure lacks that four-membered carbocyclic closure and also scores near the observed ceiling. Mean SMILES length is 57.1, ring-string incidence 0.9701, aromatic-string incidence 0.9655 and halogen-string incidence 0.9851. These recognizable aryl-amine skeletons are more conventionally medicinal than some other task outputs, but their exact stereochemistry, properties and synthesis are untested. Parent leaders are a flexible heavily halogenated tertiary diaryl amine in seed 0, an aminoethyl/pyrrolidine aryl ether in seed 1 and a cyclic thioether/pyrrolidine biaryl in seed 2. No absence of basic-amine chemistry can be inferred.
liabilities: Halogenated hydrophobic aryl regions coexist with multiple amines and unspecified stereochemistry; their supplied score is not a complete medicinal chemistry property assessment.

Aziridine, azetidine and substituted benzocyclobutene-like structures have distinct ring-strain and reactivity considerations. Their presence does not warrant treating all small rings as equally implausible.

Some seed-0 relatives use sulfur with additional C=S or S=C-like multiple-bond connectivity, whereas the leading sulfoxide has a more conventional sulfur environment; those cases must remain distinct.
missing_features: Potential stereogenic carbon centres, saturated ring junctions and the sulfoxide environment lack assigned stereochemical identity; these records do not identify the stereoisomer or conformation responsible for a score.
Relevant protonation states are unspecified in neutral SMILES even though protonatable centres are abundant. The missing information is chemical state definition, not a missing basic nitrogen motif.

The trajectories do not establish stability, selectivity, solubility or a synthetic route at their near-ceiling values. The open-chain near-ceiling counterexample already supplies a less constrained alternative, so strained-ring formation is not a demonstrated requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The low-scoring N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine carboxylic acid at seed 0 evaluation 30 scores 0.0002055750798690747; aromatic rings and nitrogen are therefore insufficient by themselves. The Child aryl/amine leaders reach 0.9782025295627597, 0.9972549276507919 and 0.999996516262112 in seeds 0, 1 and 2. In seed 1, the azetidine-to-aziridine variant scores 0.9911234263049759, while replacing that ring nitrogen with sulfur scores 0.9319313997705189. This is a local association with the exposed amine arrangement, not a universal small-ring optimum. In seed 2, the earlier open-chain diarylmethylamino/pyrrolidine scores 0.9999817933180638; its hydroxylated diazine-ring relative falls to 0.5772926812703653. Adding aromatic nitrogens is not generically beneficial. The late benzocyclobutene-like leader without the extra primary amino substituent already scores 0.9999960240536364, so that extra amino group is not shown to be necessary for the near-ceiling value. Observed Child versus matched Parent best values are: seed 0, 0.9782025295627597 versus 0.9999989177995104; seed 1, 0.9972549276507919 versus 0.9969753164881906; seed 2, 0.999996516262112 versus 0.9999934235240012. The visible common feature is a whole aryl/aliphatic-amine arrangement, not measured binding or a unique required ring system.

per_task.generated_character: The output is rich in aromatic and nitrogen-carbonyl frameworks but only modestly scored. Seed 0's 36-heavy-atom best links ethoxy-substituted phenyl and tolyl regions through nitrogen-containing medium rings with N-methyl groups, two carbonyls and N-N connectivity; graph cycles include seven- and eight-membered rings. Seed 1's 32-heavy-atom best connects a propyl/ethoxyphenyl group to a densely bridged diaryl nitrogen-dicarbonyl core. Close members insert N-N or carbon-containing links into that core. Seed 2's 34-heavy-atom best joins an unusual aromatic-labelled nitrogen-rich ring to an aryl aza-ketone region through an N-O-alkyl connection and also contains an N-methyl lactam-like ring. Its consecutive nitrogen atoms and medium-ring graph are not a conventional simple aza-aromatic scaffold. Mean proposal SMILES length is 56.0, aromatic-string incidence 0.9713, ring-string incidence 0.9782 and halogen-string incidence only 0.1402. Thus missing halogen or missing rings is not a supported explanation. Parent seeds retain related aromatic/bridged nitrogen-carbonyl territory, including quinoline-linked dicarbonyl/ether ring systems. Recognizable individual functions coexist with difficult topology and unresolved stereochemistry on both sides.
liabilities: Multiple medium-ring bridges and ring-bound unsaturation can make synthesis and geometry difficult even at moderate heavy-atom counts.
N-N and N-O linkages, including consecutive nitrogen atoms in an aromatic-labelled region, require local chemical assessment rather than being counted as generic beneficial heteroatoms.
Unassigned centres and topologically elaborate structures recur, while single-atom and tiny unsaturated fragments still consume observed evaluations at the score floor.
missing_features: Accessible alternative connectivities that preserve the favorable aromatic/nitrogen-carbonyl arrangement without dense medium-ring bridges are not established among the strongest observed molecules.
The bridged and substituted saturated centres lack explicit stereochemical or conformational definition. Aromatic labels in the nitrogen-rich seed-2 graph do not supply that missing information.

Chemically independent, plausible high-scoring alternatives within each seed are limited even though different seeds explore different ring families. The evidence does not support an absolute inability to reorganize a scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329, while the Child best values are 0.21295611130358405, 0.21918924671407988 and 0.2141386914798737 for seeds 0, 1 and 2. Acetylene scores 0.0. The signal therefore favors combined aromatic/nitrogen-carbonyl context over tiny fragments, but shows no exact missing pharmacophore. Contracting the seed-0 medium-ring dicarbonyl relative gives 0.21108861061281722; the seed-2 contracted lactam-like relative gives 0.21225222340726826. These narrow differences do not show a general benefit from greater ring size. Seed-1 N-N and carbon-linked variants both score 0.21899032330955367, slightly below the differently attached 0.21918924671407988 leader. Inserting another nitrogen into a nearby bridge gives 0.2113438675866706, so additional nitrogen is not monotonically rewarded. Observed Child versus matched Parent best values are: seed 0, 0.21295611130358405 versus 0.2258403994203931; seed 1, 0.21918924671407988 versus 0.2214095461892601; seed 2, 0.2141386914798737 versus 0.22600312875247064. All matched Child best values are lower, within related broad chemical territory; changed topology and score remain associated observations rather than a component explanation.

per_task.generated_character: The successful regions are compact fluorinated nitrogen-carbonyl structures, but the three seed families differ sharply. Seed 0's 28-heavy-atom best combines a fused nitrogen dione, fluoromethyl substitution, a fluorinated saturated oxygen ring and a phenolic aromatic-labelled region with a short internal cross-link producing four-membered graph cycles. Seed 1's 30-heavy-atom best is a densely bridged carbonyl/urea-like polycycle with N-N bonds, N-F, carbon-bound fluorines, a fluoromethyl group, a hydroxylated diene region and an aryl thiol. Seed 2's 28-heavy-atom best is a fused nitrogen dione joined to a fluorinated bridged unsaturated carbocyclic region bearing a primary amino group; it contains ordinary separated C=C bonds and no N-F bond. A strong nearby seed-2 example opens that extra bridging into a substituted seven-membered diene ring but introduces N-F. Mean SMILES length is 52.2, ring-string incidence 0.9598, aromatic-string incidence 0.9483, halogen-string incidence 0.8828 and cumulated-double-bond-string incidence 0.023. The leader therefore does not reproduce the Parent seed-2 small-ring cumulene hazard, although topology and stereochemistry remain unresolved. Parent seed 0 uses an N-fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycle with a small unsaturated nitrogen ring, Parent seed 1 a less bridged fluorinated dione, and Parent seed 2 the cyclic-cumulene/large aromatic-labelled nitrogen-ring family.
liabilities: The seed-0 aromatic-labelled short cross-links and seed-1 crowded bridged topology have unresolved geometric plausibility despite accepted scores.
N-F and N-N environments plus an aryl thiol occur in the seed-1 leader; neither the conventional label urea nor its score establishes stability of the whole polycycle.

The fluorinated seed-2 diene bridges avoid a carbon-centred cumulene but still create multiple unassigned centres and difficult ring connectivity. The less-bridged high-scoring counterexample retains a separate N-F concern.
missing_features: Geometrically credible, synthetically accessible alternatives preserving the favorable compact fluorinated dione arrangement are not consistently demonstrated. The seed-2 top molecule avoids the Parent cyclic cumulene and N-F, so those liabilities cannot be treated as unavoidable generator outputs.

Potential stereogenic fluorinated carbons, ring junctions and amino-bearing centres lack explicit stereochemical identity; the trajectories do not identify a preferred tautomer, conformer or stereoisomer.

The higher reward for a particular dione/fluorine/amino arrangement does not reveal an absent exact pharmacophore. Extra amino substitution and a thione replacement provide strong counterexamples to simplistic functional-group prescriptions.

In seed 0, extending the saturated oxygen ring by one carbon lowers 0.42248772984058786 to 0.21435073283939884. In seed 2, changing one dione oxygen to sulfur gives 0.00021901608523897876; changing one carbon-bound fluorine to amino gives 0.001778564838545041. Those close counterexamples support sensitivity to the complete polar-group composition and placement, not a general benefit from more donors or arbitrary heteroatom replacement. Isolated fluorine scores 1.1043196211273875e-26, and the final seed-2 vinylamine proposal scores 2.365058330274635e-17: fluorine or amine functionality alone does not recreate the successful context. Observed Child versus matched Parent best values are: seed 0, 0.42248772984058786 versus 0.6510211907030741; seed 1, 0.5959013456438182 versus 0.4870057305679067; seed 2, 0.6464670514720593 versus 0.7208853668418119. The seed-1 improvement and seed-0/seed-2 losses retain their opposite directions; they do not show that one topology or N-F status universally controls reward.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source and conditions: this gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in Parent n-62daf219c70a; it recurs in n-60350f969287 under the epoch-1 profile, Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per task and feedback batches of 10. Current leaders include N-F/N-Br/N-Cl aromatic or cyclic nitrogen, N-amino amides, and unoxidized S-F attachments. Counterexamples are essential: an earlier conventional diarylmethylamino/pyrrolidine reaches 0.9999817933180638, the fluorinated dione leader at 0.6464670514720593 contains no N-F, and changing one peripheral S-F to S-methyl accompanies a slightly higher observed value. The problem is inconsistent environment control, not inability to emit useful amines, carbon-bound halogens or conventional sulfur chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while modifying otherwise useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need chemically meaningful local alternatives that preserve favorable complete scaffold relationships learned from real feedback, while distinguishing carbon-bound halogens, N-halogen bonds, ordinary thioethers/sulfoxides and unoxidized sulfur fluorides. These examples motivate assessing bond environments; they do not establish that a universal halogen or heteroatom filter raises reward, or that any particular search component caused the liability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source and conditions: n-c55c3d520a2c and its same-output Parent baseline n-62daf219c70a established this chemical concern on the supplied Search panel. It is re-observed in n-60350f969287 under epoch 1 at the same Search seeds, observation budget and batch size. The current evidence is not an unchanged Parent cyclic-cumulene leader: it includes short internal cross-links in aromatic-labelled fragments, nitrogen-rich medium-ring bridges and crowded fluorinated diene polycycles. Conversely, conventional saturated cyclic amines and a less-bridged diene analogue at 0.6368477634260005 remain strongly scored. Successful graph parsing, many ring digits and aromatic labels do not demonstrate an accessible three-dimensional structure.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish representable ring connectivity from credible geometry and synthetically accessible topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need awareness of ring size, unsaturation, bridge connectivity and plausible conformational alternatives while retaining favorable functional relationships. Distinguish ordinary small rings from unsupported aromatic cross-links or constrained unsaturation. The chemical concern is conditional; a blanket ban on small rings, all bridges or ring formation is not supported, and chemistry association does not identify mechanism contribution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source and conditions: the same representation gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a and persists for n-60350f969287 across the complete supplied Search panel under epoch 1. Every current task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0 despite amino-ether methines, substituted small rings, fluorinated bridgeheads and a sulfoxide among the observed molecules. Charged-string incidence is also 0.0, but accessible aliphatic amines are visibly present. No stereochemical penalty, protonation failure or preferred isomer is established by these scalar scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemical identity after generating potentially stereogenic saturated, bridged and sulfur-containing environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations need to preserve or explicitly resolve configurational identity when the resulting chemistry requires it, with separate handling of achiral and configurationally unstable cases. Protonation and tautomerism are separate state questions. The absent specification is directly observed; a score benefit from resolving it and attribution to any component remain unmeasured.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source and conditions: this conditional gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c, is preserved in n-62daf219c70a, and recurs in n-60350f969287 at the supplied epoch-1 Search budget. Late tiny halogen or hydrocarbon observations reach recorded floors; a final vinylamine is also extremely low. At the other extreme, an 80-heavy-atom elaboration scores 0.6038062283737025, below the related 45-heavy-atom best at 0.6042806936682606. Yet compact aryl amines score highly, and smaller complete heteroaryl arrangements are already generated. The evidence concerns retention of a whole useful arrangement, not a universal minimum or maximum size.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain useful functional-group context while avoiding unhelpful fragmentation and repeated structural elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local feedback should support transformations that preserve enough chemical context to test the learned arrangement while allowing meaningful simplification or replacement. Check whether elaboration retains useful relationships rather than merely adding repeated rings, and whether fragmentation leaves a viable whole candidate. No fixed size cutoff or guaranteed benefit from greater size follows from these observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source and conditions: leading-family concentration was documented for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a and remains a conditional coverage concern for n-60350f969287 under the complete epoch-1 Search panel. Leaders repeatedly vary alkyl, halogen, carbonyl-adjacent or short ring segments on a retained family. The strongest aromatic/carbonyl family differs across seeds, as do compact heteroaryl, very large repeated heteroaryl, aryl-amine and fluorinated-polycycle arrangements; this is not global structural collapse or lack of ring generation. Close counterexamples show that more nitrogen, more carbon or a sulfur-for-oxygen replacement can lower score, so merely changing atoms is not reliable useful scaffold breadth.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently supply chemically independent, plausible alternatives to the leading scaffold family within each seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Scaffold-level alternatives need to preserve feedback-supported whole functional and spatial relationships in chemically distinct, feasible connectivities, with usefulness judged from subsequent real labels. Distinct strings, ring counts and global diversity do not certify useful alternatives. These chemical coverage observations neither establish that more diversity improves the objective nor attribute the observed concentration to the removed source-identity exclusion.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
